data.title: Anthropic's Blockbuster IPO Dominated Headlines This Week – AI Anxiety Eased, While Investors And Employees Reaped A Windfall
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic stock closed 17% higher on its first trading day, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $1.8 trillion.
  • Anthropic’s co-founders’ stakes were each valued at roughly $20 billion, while employees held about $232 billion in equity, or around $44 million per employee on average, according to Reuters. 
  • Nvidia topped Q3 expectations and said it does not plan to reinstate Huang as CEO.

Anthropic (ANT) dominated tech headlines this week with the largest IPO in history, while Nvidia (NVDA) also drew attention due to its earnings report.

Anthropic saw incredible demand for its IPO, and the stock popped on debut. Meanwhile, Nvidia reported another set of strong earnings even as the fallout from former CEO Jensen Huang’s departure continued to weigh on sentiment for the AI chipmakers.

Here’re the major developments from the week so far:

Anthropic Rises On Debut After Blockbuster IPO

ANT stock closed 17% higher on the first day, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $1.8 trillion. However, shares tumbled 6% in premarket trading on Friday, weighing on tech stocks. Analysts believe Anthropic’s growth, enterprise demand and model capabilities could drive further gains, though its heavy infrastructure costs and valuation remain key concerns.

About 68% of some 17,500 retail traders who voted in a Stocktwits poll said they had planned to avoid the stock on the debut day.

Anthropic Delivers Windfall For Investors, Employees

Anthropic’s IPO created enormous paper wealth. Its seven co-founders’ stakes were each valued at roughly $20 billion, while employees held about $232 billion in equity, or around $44 million per employee on average, according to Reuters.

Top investors Menlo Ventures, Spark Capital, and Lightspeed, among others, saw the value of their investment grow manyfold.

Nvidia Posts Another Record Quarter, Says No Plan To Reinstate Huang

Nvidia’s Q3 sales more than doubled to $115.8 billion, beating expectations, according to results issued on Tuesday. Revenue from the all-important data center segment rose 110% to $107.6 billion, also higher than targets.

The chipmaker raised its forecast revenue growth for fiscal 2028 from 70% to 75%.

Nvidia said it did not plan to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, who had earlier expressed a desire to return, and would continue the search for his replacement.

California Probes Nvidia

California opened an investigation into whether former CEO Jensen Huang’s actions allowed China to obtain advanced AI technology and misled investors, the state’s attorney general Rob Bonta announced on Thursday.

Meanwhile, lawmakers disclosed that the Commerce Department had approved sales of more than 800,000 advanced AI chips to Chinese firms through May, including companies on the Pentagon’s list of Chinese military firms.

The developments add to the Nvidia fallout as investors reassess their positions in a post-Huang era.

How Did Tech Stocks Move This Week?

Nebius (NBIS) and CoreWeave (CRWV) were the top tech losers in the Nasdaq-100 through Thursday, falling nearly 25% each. Palo Alto Networks (PANW) was the biggest gainer, up 12%.

The Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) lost 1.3%.

data.title: Japan's bank shares slide even as Ueda vows more rate rises
data.description:
Japanese bank shares fell on November 19 even as Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament that the central bank would keep raising interest rates.

The TOPIX Banks index opened 2.1% lower, Saxo Bank said, and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group , the country's biggest lender, opened 3.1% down. MUFG recovered to close 1.7% lower, its sixth straight daily fall. Mizuho Financial Group shed 2.1% and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group 0.8%, while the broader TOPIX ended flat and the Nikkei 225 gained 0.7%.

Ueda was presenting the central bank's twice-yearly report to the upper house's Committee on Financial Affairs. Underlying inflation 'is at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent', he told the committee, and with financial conditions still accommodative 'the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation'. The policy rate has stood at 1.25% since September, up from minus 0.1% at the start of 2024.

Rising rates ought to be a windfall for lenders that spent a decade earning next to nothing on deposits. Japan's bank stocks, though, now trade less on where the policy rate is heading than on each lurch in the government bond market, and the past month has supplied several.

Bank of Japan policy rate and 10-year government bond yield, %, January 2024 to October 2026. Source: BIS, OECD via IntelliNews Lambda

Weak auction, strong auction

A day before Ueda spoke, the Ministry of Finance's sale of 20-year bonds drew bids of JPY1.91 trillion ($12.0bn) for the JPY525.8bn ($3.3bn) it accepted, a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.64. The October sale had attracted 5.84, the highest in the ministry's records going back to 1987, and the previous 12 auctions averaged 3.92. The tail, the gap between the average and lowest accepted prices, widened to 0.29 from 0.07.

Saxo Bank put the result down to 'reduced appetite for duration amid rising inflation expectations'.

A strong sale has hurt the banks as well. After October's record demand, bond futures rallied, long-term yields eased and the banking sub-index fell more than 3% that afternoon, Kabutan reported, as traders bet the climb in domestic rates might pause. Lenders treated by the market as rate plays are being sold when yields look set to stall and again when buyers of government debt hold back.

Bid-to-cover ratio at 20-year Japanese government bond auctions, January 2025 to November 18, 2026. Source: Ministry of Finance, Japan. IntelliNews

Paper losses and a leak

Valuation losses on yen-denominated bonds have been growing as rates climb, particularly at regional and shinkin banks with large holdings, the Bank of Japan said in its October Financial System Report. Word that the Financial Services Agency would examine shinkin banks' bond portfolios emerged in September, days after the 10-year yield touched 3% for the first time in three decades.

At MUFG, higher rates are already paying off. Its net interest income rose to JPY1.85 trillion ($11.6bn) in the six months to September from JPY1.44 trillion a year earlier, and net profit climbed 26.1% to JPY1.63 trillion ($10.2bn), its investor presentation shows. The group lifted its full-year profit target to JPY2.8 trillion ($17.5bn) from JPY2.7 trillion and added a buyback of up to JPY200bn ($1.25bn).

The paper loss on its JPY12.38 trillion ($77.4bn) of government bonds was a modest JPY0.13 trillion ($813mn). Its shares still fell 3.75% on November 17, the day it presented those numbers to investors.

MUFG Bank, the group's main lender, disclosed on November 18 that a breach at Plaid, a contractor whose KARTE service it uses for website and app messaging, had exposed the gender, age and home region of about 6.5mn customers, though not names or contact details. Nikkei tied the sixth consecutive fall in the shares to the leak. Japanese lenders were already tightening identity checks after a run of data breaches elsewhere.

The 160 line

The yen weakened past 160 per dollar on November 12 for the first time since early September, and the ECB's reference rates put it at 159.97 on November 19. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama told reporters on November 13 that the market was seeing rapid, one-sided moves and that Tokyo would keep working closely with the US Treasury and respond appropriately. The ministry bought JPY15.4 trillion ($96.3bn) of yen between July 30 and August 3, its intervention records show.

A cheap yen feeds the inflation Ueda wants to pin down. He told lawmakers that the currency's fall so far would push up prices, mainly of durable goods, and that the risk was of underlying inflation overshooting 2%. For the banks that argues for more rate rises, and for a longer stretch in which the bonds on their books lose value.

Japanese yen per US dollar, end of month, January 2024 to October 2026, and November 19, 2026. Source: BIS, ECB via IntelliNews Lambda

Investors are not doubting that Japanese rates will go higher. They are pricing what comes with that: a bond market that wobbles more often, paper losses that land hardest on smaller lenders, and a currency that could force Tokyo's hand. MUFG's profits are rising fast, yet its shares have lost 8.7% in six sessions.

data.title: RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RLX Technology Inc. ("RLX Technology" or the "Company") (), a leading global branded e-vapor company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Gross profit increased by 26.7% to RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026.
  • Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.
  • Non-GAAP income from operations[1] was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP net income[1] was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

"The third quarter marked a defining inflection point for RLX as we integrated our newly acquired European distribution platform with our existing retail footprint, evolving into a leading global smoke-free brand," said Ms. Ying (Kate) Wang, Co-founder, Chairperson, and Chief Executive Officer of RLX Technology. "We now possess end-to-end capabilities spanning global product innovation, supply chain execution, and direct route-to-market reach, while always placing our brands at the heart of adult consumers' choices worldwide. By pairing these strengths with dedicated local field teams and an open, multi-brand ecosystem philosophy, we are gaining sharper retail insights that will empower us to tailor products to local consumer preferences, scale our multi-category portfolio, and capture market share as shifting global regulations reshape the industry."

Mr. Chao Lu, Chief Financial Officer of RLX Technology, commented, "We delivered strong third quarter financial results, with the consolidation driving a surge in net revenues to RMB1.92 billion, up 69.7% year over year. International markets contributed 86.5% of our top line. While our blended gross margin now reflects the consolidation of the distribution business, we maintained solid non-GAAP profitability, improved working capital efficiency, and achieved a healthy sequential rebound in operating cash flow. Looking ahead, we are actively lifting our European platform's margins through supply chain optimization and capital deployment, while navigating transitional working capital needs related to the UK's October introduction of an excise duty. Supported by RMB13.48 billion in total financial assets, we have the financial flexibility to fund global brand expansion, deliver long-term sustainable growth, and maintain strong shareholder returns."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity in July 2026. Net revenues from international business represented 86.5% of net revenues for the period.

Gross profit was RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 26.7% from RMB352.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.

Operating expenses were RMB407.1 million (US$60.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB259.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and increased shipping and logistics costs.

Selling expenses were RMB182.9 million (US$27.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB132.3 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increases in salary and welfare expenses and shipping and logistics costs.

General and administrative expenses were RMB185.9 million (US$27.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB85.7 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and legal and other consulting fees.

Research and development expenses were RMB38.3 million (US$5.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB41.3 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP income from operations was RMB39.5 million (US$5.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB93.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Income tax expense was RMB43.6 million (US$6.5 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB45.9 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP net income was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per American depositary share ("ADS") were RMB0.131 (US$0.020) and RMB0.123 (US$0.018), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.167 and RMB0.157, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS[2] were RMB0.186 (US$0.028) and RMB0.175 (US$0.026), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.236 and RMB0.221, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

For more information on the Company's non-GAAP financial measures, please see the section "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and the table captioned "Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" set forth at the end of this press release.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term bank deposits, net, short-term investments, long-term bank deposits, net, and long-term investment securities, net, of RMB13,482.8 million (US$2,011.0 million), compared with RMB13,883.4 million as of June 30, 2026. data.title: Hacksaw Gaming Enters Delaware with BetRivers
data.description:
Hacksaw Gaming is pleased to announce its entry into Delaware. The company is launching an initial selection of its acclaimed slot portfolio with BetRivers, an online casino brand of Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI). The launch brings Hacksaw titles to players in the state for the first time and marks another milestone in the company’s US expansion.

In October 2026, Hacksaw Gaming obtained approval as a Gaming Vendor from the Delaware Lottery. This paved the way for its entry into the locally licensed market through BetRivers, which operates online gaming in Delaware on behalf of the Delaware Lottery.

Philippa Gregory, Operational CEO of Hacksaw Gaming, commented:

“Going live in Delaware with BetRivers is a fantastic milestone for Hacksaw Gaming and another important step in our US expansion. RSI was our very first partner in the US, and we’ve built a great relationship with the team over the years. Building on our successful launches together in West Virginia and New Jersey, we’re delighted to be bringing our games to players in Delaware and continuing to grow our presence across the US.”

The launch adds Delaware to Hacksaw Gaming’s growing network of locally licensed US markets, which now includes six states: Connecticut, Delaware, Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia.

For more information, please contact:

E-mail: ir@hacksawgroup.com

About Hacksaw

Hacksaw AB (publ) is a B2B technology platform and game development company. The scalable and modular platform, built on a modern code base, enables rapid development and distribution of games. Games developed by Hacksaw comprise digital slots, scratch cards, crash games and prediction market infrastructure solutions designed for gaming operators and other qualified businesses. We operate across the whole B2B iGaming value chain, from game development to distribution and our customers comprise some of the largest private and state-owned iGaming operators in the industry. Hacksaw’s shares are listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (HACK).

data.title: India's RBI expected to raise rates in December, deliver final hike in February
data.description:
Key points:
  • RBI to raise repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% on December 4, say 56 of 61 economists
  • Majority expect final hike to 6% in February as inflation tops target

By Pranoy Krishna

The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to raise its key interest rate to 5.75% on December 4, followed by a final hike in February, a Reuters poll of economists showed, as inflation breaches the upper end of the central bank's 2%-6% target band.

An energy price shock triggered by the war in the Middle East, coupled with uneven and deficient monsoon rainfall, pushed inflation past the RBI's 6% threshold in October for the first time in two years.

Other major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, are also expected to raise rates in December to fight persistently high inflation.

With India's economic growth expected to remain strong, the RBI, which kick-started its rate-hiking cycle last month, has room to tighten policy further, analysts say.

More than 90% of economists, 56 of 61, in a November 13-20 Reuters poll forecast the RBI to hike its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% at the conclusion of its December 2-4 policy meeting.

While three economists expected the central bank to leave rates unchanged, two predicted a larger 50-basis-point increase.

A majority of economists, 34 of 46, also forecast the RBI to follow up with a final hike to 6% in February.

"The inflation outlook has deteriorated in the last few months ... the fact that India is growing much faster than we had expected — could be north of 8% easily — I think that gives the RBI more latitude to prioritise elevated inflation, which has now breached the upper end of the tolerance range," said Dhiraj Nim, senior economist at ANZ.

"There is a clear generalisation of pressures beyond transitory parts of CPI, which are energy and food."

Despite a recent decline in crude oil , prices are nearly 30% above prewar levels, suggesting inflation will remain elevated in the near term.

However, the rupee's turnaround from one of Asia's worst-performing currencies to one of its best-performing could give the RBI space to moderate the pace of tightening. The central bank has spent billions of dollars to defend the currency against the dollar this year.

Still, a cumulative 75-basis-point increase would mark the shallowest tightening cycle in more than eight years.

"The chatter around aggressive rate hikes was only building up because the rupee was under significant pressure just a month ago. At this point, they (RBI) will be a little more comfortable," said Upasna Bharadwaj, chief economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, who expects two more rate hikes.

Bharadwaj added inflation would remain elevated and closer to the 6% mark for the next five to six months.

While inflation was forecast to average 6% in the fourth quarter and come down in the subsequent quarters, it was expected to stay above the RBI's medium-term target of 4% this year and next — a view broadly unchanged from the October poll.

Elevated prices will weigh on household spending and slow economic activity over the coming quarters.

The economy likely grew about 8% on average over the past five quarters, including the one just ended, but is expected to slow to 6.9% this quarter and 6.8% next, the survey showed.

"Growth is improving purely because of government expenditure and, to a certain extent, because of urban consumption ... But (from) this quarter onwards, I don't think these two stories will play as much," said Debopam Chaudhuri, chief economist at Piramal Group.

data.title: Global Bond Yields Fall as Investors Seek Safe-Haven Assets — Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru

Yields on U.S., U.K., and eurozone government bonds dropped on Friday as risk-off sentiment continued to drive demand to safe-haven assets.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.6 basis points to 4.996%, while the U.K. 10-year yield dropped 4.5 bps to 5.271%, according to Tradeweb. Ten-year German Bund yields declined 6.2 bps to 3.339%.

A record initial public offering by Anthropic, which raised $81 billion, failed to revive appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks. Investors continued to question whether the enormous investments in the AI industry would pay off given the rising public resistance toward the industry.

"The blockbuster debut [IPO] couldn't sweep those worries under the rug," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said in a note.

Asian and European stocks sold off on Friday as sentiment continued to deteriorate even after some positive news in the tech industry this week.

"When neither a blockbuster Nvidia beat nor the largest IPO in history can lift the tape, market psychology has fundamentally flipped from dip-buying to structural de-risking," Patrick Munnelly, partner at Tickmill Group, said in a note.

High borrowing costs also raise concerns about AI companies' ability to continue raising funds to finance their massive expansion.

"The scale of the Democratic win in the midterm [elections] has deepened worry that policymakers could push for slower data-center spending," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said in a note.

The concerns about the tech and AI sector are driving the flight to safety, causing government bond yields to drop, Groman said.

data.title: Japan Tobacco cuts dividend by a quarter after losing control in Russia
data.description:
Japanese cigarette maker Japan Tobacco has cut its 2026 dividend by a quarter after losing control of its Russian business, the company said on November 19.

The board cut the final payout to JPY68 ($0.43) a share from the JPY136 ($0.85) it had planned in July, bringing the full-year dividend to JPY204 ($1.28) against a forecast of JPY272 ($1.70), according to its revised forecast filed with the Tokyo Stock Exchange. The chairman, the vice-chairman and three representative directors will take a 50% cut in base pay for two months, and the representative directors will forgo their 2026 bonuses.

The dividend cut will also reduce income for the Japanese state, which owns about 37% of Japan Tobacco. The Finance Ministry received JPY156bn ($975mn) in dividends for the previous financial year, according to Reuters, as reported by IntelliNews. Japan Tobacco appears to be the first Japanese group caught by the Kremlin's temporary-management regime for foreign-owned assets.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi raised the protection of Japanese business interests with President Vladimir Putin when they met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on November 18, Bloomberg reported, citing Japan's foreign ministry. It was the first face-to-face meeting between the two countries' leaders in seven years. Tokyo has protested through diplomatic channels and called for the decision to be reversed.

Putin's decrees of November 5 and November 6 put all seven of the group's Russian subsidiaries under the temporary management of Moscow-based Industrial Assets. The first covered the factory companies Petro in St Petersburg and JTI Donskoy Tabak in Rostov-on-Don and the leaf processors JTI Yelets in the Lipetsk region and Cres Neva in the Leningrad region. The second added the sales company JTI Russia, the dormant Pereslavl-Tabak and J.T.I. Innovative Products, which sold Ploom heated-tobacco devices.

The regime leaves Japan Tobacco with legal title but stops it taking operating decisions, so under IFRS the group deconsolidated the seven companies with effect from November 6 and expects to book a loss of about JPY1.377 trillion ($8.6bn) on losing control. About JPY1.5 trillion ($9.4bn) of assets, including goodwill, and JPY200bn ($1.25bn) of liabilities leave its balance sheet, along with about JPY400bn ($2.5bn) in cash.

The deconsolidation does not mean giving up ownership, selling the business or leaving Russia, where the local companies are still trading, chief executive Takehiko Tsutsui and chief financial officer Hiromasa Furukawa told investors in a presentation on November 19. The company said it would take every possible step to protect its rights and assets.

Japan Tobacco now expects a 2026 operating loss of JPY368bn ($2.3bn) instead of a JPY1.041 trillion ($6.5bn) profit, and a net loss of JPY724bn ($4.5bn) where it had forecast a JPY662bn ($4.1bn) profit. It cut its revenue forecast to JPY3.84 trillion ($24bn) from JPY3.903 trillion ($24.4bn). Before the decrees, Russia was expected to provide about 10% of group revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit this year.

The group will aim for a payout ratio of about 70% from 2027, at the bottom of its 75% plus or minus five points policy range, and expects adjusted operating profit at constant exchange rates to grow by more than 10% a year in 2027-29 on a basis that excludes Russia, with the dividend rising from JPY204.

Japan Tobacco has been in Russia since 1999, when it bought the international business of RJ Reynolds. Its brands there include Winston, Camel, LD, Sobranie and Mevius, and it estimated its share of the Russian cigarette market at 36.9% at the end of 2025, Forbes Russia reported.

Piper Sandler maintained Intuit at Underweight and lowered its price target to $270 from $290, a 6.9% decrease.

The price target implies a downside of 12.9% from the Nov 19 close of $310.02.
